profile.reading: This building is one of two structures making up SFO1, part of Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster at 2401 and 2403 Walsh Avenue in Santa Clara, California. Csquare, Inc., trading on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR, is the current name of a data center real estate company with a documented and unusually well-sourced corporate history. Its OpenStreetMap tag for this exact building was updated in December 2025 from operator CenturyLink, itself a 2016-era tag, to Centersquare and then, hours later the same day, to the current Csquare, a sequence that mirrors the company own real rebrand path: these Silicon Valley facilities trace back to CenturyLink Savvis-heritage colocation assets, which were divested and became Evoque Data Center Solutions around 2020 to 2021 under Brookfield-affiliated ownership, later rebranded Centersquare, and rebranded again to Csquare ahead of its July 16, 2026 initial public offering. That IPO priced at 21 dollars per share across 50 million shares for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross, and Brookfield Corporation retained approximately 69 percent of voting power afterward, making Csquare a controlled company under NYSE rules. Per Csquare own SEC registration prospectus, the company overall portfolio as of March 31, 2026 spanned 64 sites across 21 major metro markets in the US, Canada, and the UK, totaling roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity and more than 1,700 customers. That same prospectus Properties table lists two Silicon Valley buildings under the SFO1 code, designated SFO1_A at 60,982 rentable square feet, 64.9 percent occupied, and SFO1_B at 38,634 rentable square feet, 63.9 percent occupied, both company-owned, though which specific street address corresponds to which suffix could not be confirmed this session, so no single building-level square footage figure is assigned to this record individually.

reading.body:
Csquare SFO1 in Santa Clara publishes 129.4 MW of combined utility power, which ranks it outside the top ten of California's published data center capacity even as one of only eleven facilities statewide to publish a power figure at all. The operator claims 34.5 MW of IT capacity across 95,981 square feet of raised floor, which at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack would support roughly 860 racks, though this site publishes no tenant list or actual utilization.

The campus holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and NIST 800-53 certifications, qualifying it for security-sensitive workloads, and carries LEED certification. The operator, Csquare, operates a portfolio of 80 data centers with more than 500 MW of total capacity across 15 North American markets, placing this single facility as part of a distributed regional footprint rather than a purpose-built AI hub.

Silicon Valley's grid and real estate constraints mean that 34.5 MW of IT capacity in a single campus is material for non-AI enterprise workloads but is smaller than single-purpose AI clusters now coming online elsewhere. The site publishes no expansion roadmap or power escalation plan, leaving its future relevance to AI scaling undeclared.
